note: 4.3-N1 candidate pool and the role of overnight_return_open
statement: This note was written after the 4.3.4-4.3.9 run and records two decisions. Because it changes two sentences of amendment A3, it acts as the dated amendment that A3 requires for any change.

1_candidate_pool.rule: The adjusted columns (<name>__sadj) join the candidate pool alongside their raw columns. The pool is the 80 raw columns plus the 36 adjusted columns, 116 in all.
1_candidate_pool.eligibility: An adjusted column inherits the eligibility of its raw column. 4.3.4 found no slot with an undefined or non-positive median in either era, so adjusted coverage equals raw coverage. 10 of the 20 primary columns are scale features, so their adjusted versions are primary-eligible.
supersedes_in_A3: rules.4.3.7_eligibility.adjusted_columns: 'an adjusted column follows the eligibility of its raw column and is not a separate candidate' (now: it follows the eligibility but is a separate candidate)
rules.4.3.8_redundancy.applies_to: 'raw columns of each eligibility set separately'

2_overnight.rule: overnight_return_open is response-side only: it may appear only on the response side (as an outcome or label variable) of the later overnight analysis, and never as a detector input, feature, scaler input or HMM input. This restates and keeps the A2 exclusion.

not_done: No eligibility or redundancy statistic was computed for the 116-column pool. The 4.3.7 and 4.3.8 outputs stay exactly as produced, on the 80 raw columns.
Raw/adjusted pairs were not correlated here; any redundancy rule for the 116-column pool needs a new dated rule before it is run.
The overnight analysis is still not specified.
unchanged: the 80 raw detector columns and their frozen matrix
